Soft pneumatic arm · controller tests · make_calibrated_sim seed 0

Test Motion Results

Every controller from scripts/compare_controllers.py, with its gains unchanged (tuned on the scored 7 mm, 0.1 Hz circle), on the three test motions of the course project brief (axial, circular, triangular). Plant: make_calibrated_sim(control_hz=100, seed=0), 0.5 s dead time and 0.6 s pressure lag. 5 s settle at 4.5 psi, then 30 s of tracking, scored like evaluate_controller.

Summary

  • The delay-aware SMC and NDOSMC (M2) have the lowest error on every brief motion: 2.1–3.5 mm planar RMSE.
  • At 0.4–0.5 Hz the motions are hard. A controller that holds the arm still scores 3.0–8.9 mm. Several controllers do worse than that, and the delay-aware SMC beats it only narrowly on the axial motion (2.67 vs 2.99 mm).
  • The delay-aware SMC wins on phase, not shape. On the 4.3 mm circle it traces a circle of about 7 mm radius and switches its commands between 0 and 9 psi.
  • On the slow triangle (7.5 s per lap) the delay-aware controllers, the paper SMC and Nikoletta's corrected SMC tie at 2.05–2.08 mm.
  • On the lab's recorded real-robot runs (0.1 Hz) the delay-aware controllers are also best: 1.1–1.6 mm.

Commands at 0 or 9 psi, delay-aware SMC: 21 / 35 / 81 / 36 / 3 %; PD and Nikoletta's SMC about 0 %. z RMSE where z is in the reference (axial, open-loop circle): delay-aware SMC 0.32 / 0.52 mm, PD corrected 0.86 / 0.97 mm. Max error, phase lag and every value above: docs/figures/benchmark_slide_tasks.json.

Read these numbers with three facts in mind

  • The delay and lag add up to 1.1 s. At 0.4 Hz that is 0.44 of a lap, so a controller without prediction tracks half a cycle late. The "delayed and lagged" row shows what that alone costs.
  • The delay-aware SMC overshoots on the fast circles and the open-loop ellipse (last lap reaches about 11 mm in y against 7.8 mm). One likely cause, not yet tested: its reference preview r + Tṙ + ½T²r̈ is a Taylor series, and at 0.4 Hz with T = 0.5 s it makes a circle about 27 % too large (|1 + iωT − (ωT)²/2| = 1.27 for ωT = 1.26).
  • Nikoletta's SMC as written beats the corrected λ = 8 version on all four fast motions. That has not been investigated.

These runs compare controllers with each other, not with hardware. The model-based controllers saturate 20–59 % of commands. uv run python scripts/benchmark_all_tasks.py, docs/figures/benchmark_all_tasks.json.

Actuator delay check

The controllers use T = 0.50 s and τ = 0.60 s, identified from simulator data (grid search over T, least squares for gain and τ; fit error 0.005 psi). The same fit on the real robot's commanded vs measured pressure (16 segment-runs) gives:

  • T + τ = 0.81–1.44 s, centred near 1.1 s, which agrees with 0.5 + 0.6 s.
  • T alone ranges 0.20–0.75 s and τ 0.19–1.10 s. At 0.1 Hz a dead time and a lag both appear as phase, so this data cannot separate them.
  • Fit error 0.2–0.8 psi (10–20 % of the signal): a dead time plus one lag describes the hardware only approximately. The triangle ramps give the longest lags.

Step tests on the hardware would separate T from τ. This check ran from a scratch script that is not in the repo yet.

Reproduce

  • uv run python scripts/benchmark_slide_tasks.py: brief motions, figures and JSON (about 90 s).
  • uv run python scripts/benchmark_all_tasks.py: recorded real-robot runs (about 4 min).
  • Hold-still row: planar RMS of each reference, computed from the same references.
